body:
[V1.5.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x10-V1-Architecture.md) describes the need for input validation enforced on a trusted service layer. It is a level 2 requirement.

[V5.1.3](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/4.0/en/0x13-V5-Validation-Sanitization-Encoding.md#v51-input-validation-requirements) requires all input is validated using positive validation. Other 5.1.X requirements also talk about input validation. All of them are ASVS level 1.

This implies that input validation is considered a level 1 requirement and input validation **on a trusted service layer** is considered a level 2 requirement. I believe that input validation NOT on a trusted service layer adds almost no security. Hense, if 5.1.x requirements are level 1 (I believe they should be), then V1.5.3 should also be level 1.

ASVS aims to make level 1 requirements blackbox-testable. I believe that a black-box test can determine if input validation occurs on a trusted service layer (aka NOT on the client-side). This does seem to invalidate the existing logic that architectural requirements are never ASVS level 1.

comments.body:
My proposal is to move current V1.5.3 to category V5.1 and change level to 1.
